title: RBAC is fail-open and the `/api/agents/*` pattern misses the bare `/api/agents` route
Auth rate limiter keys on unverified `X-Forwarded-For`, allowing brute-force bypass
`bin/teleton.js` imports `dist/cli/index.js`, which the default build never produces
body:
## Description

The published binary loads a CLI bundle that the V2 build does not create:

```js
// bin/teleton.js:1-2
#!/usr/bin/env node
await import("../dist/cli/index.js");
```

`package.json` maps `bin.teleton` to `./bin/teleton.js`, and the default `npm run build` is `build:v2`, whose last step `build:apps` only bundles `apps/agent` (`apps/agent/tsup.config.ts` → `outDir: "dist/apps/agent"`). Nothing in `build:v2` emits `dist/cli/index.js`. The only producer of that path is `build:v1` (`v1-src/tsup.config.ts` declares `"cli/index": "v1-src/cli/index.ts"` → `dist/cli/index.js`), and `build:v1` is **not** part of `build`/`build:v2` — only of `build:all`.

There are two distinct problems:
1. After the default `npm run build`, `dist/cli/index.js` does not exist, so `teleton` crashes with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
2. The V2 CLI source at `apps/cli/src/index.ts` has **no** tsup config and no build script referencing it, so it is never compiled or shipped at all — `bin/teleton.js` would resolve to the *V1* CLI (`v1-src/cli/index.ts`) even after `build:all`, not the V2 CLI.

## Impact

The package's single advertised entrypoint is broken for anyone who runs the documented `npm run build` (the V2 build): invoking `teleton` fails immediately. The V2 CLI (`teleton start`, `doctor`, `config`) is dead code that is never built. Severity **high** because the primary user-facing command is non-functional.

## Required Fix

1. Decide which CLI `bin/teleton.js` should launch (V2 `apps/cli` or V1 `v1-src/cli`) and point the import at the path that is actually built.
2. If the V2 CLI is intended: add a tsup config/entry for `apps/cli/src/index.ts` (e.g. emitting `dist/apps/cli/index.js`), wire it into `build:apps`/`build:v2`, and update `bin/teleton.js` to import that output.
3. Add a smoke test (e.g. `node bin/teleton.js --version` after a clean `npm run build`) to CI so a missing CLI bundle fails the build.

## References

- Node.js ECMAScript modules — resolution and `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`: https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html

title: CORS config is created and validated but never applied as middleware
Refresh tokens carry no `type` claim and are accepted as access tokens
body:
## Description

`createToken` mints every token with the same claim set — `sub`, `role`, `iat` and an `exp` — with no claim distinguishing an access token from a refresh token:

```ts
// packages/api/src/routes/auth.ts:28-40
async function createToken(sub, role, secret, expirySeconds): Promise<string> {
  const jwtSecret = new TextEncoder().encode(secret);
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  return new jose.SignJWT({ sub, role, iat: now })
    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: "HS256" })
    .setExpirationTime(now + expirySeconds)
    .sign(jwtSecret);
}
```

Login issues both tokens with this same function (`auth.ts:90-96`), differing only in lifetime. The auth middleware (`auth.middleware.ts:86`) and `/api/auth/refresh` (`auth.ts:181-184`) both accept any validly-signed, unexpired token without checking a token `type`/`token_use`. A refresh token is therefore a fully valid `Authorization: Bearer` access token.

## Impact

The refresh token — which is long-lived (default 7 days) and meant only to obtain new access tokens — authorizes every API call directly. This defeats the security purpose of short-lived access tokens: a leaked refresh token grants week-long API access, and there is no way to scope or selectively revoke refresh credentials. **Medium** severity (broken token design; impact bounded by the dev-only login today, but the design is unsafe for production).

## Required Fix

1. Add a distinguishing claim (e.g. `type: "access" | "refresh"` or `token_use`) when minting tokens in `createToken`/login.
2. In the auth middleware, reject tokens whose `type` is not `access`.
3. In `/api/auth/refresh`, require `type === "refresh"` before issuing a new access token.
4. Add tests asserting a refresh token is rejected on protected routes and an access token is rejected by `/refresh`.

## References

- OWASP JSON Web Token for Java Cheat Sheet (token-type / audience separation): https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/JSON_Web_Token_for_Java_Cheat_Sheet.html
- CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html

title: Body-size limit only inspects `Content-Length` and is bypassed by chunked/missing header
`startServer` registers no `error` handler, so port-in-use never settles the start promise
Swagger UI at `/api/docs` is blocked by the global CSP (CDN + inline scripts)
body:
## Description

The security-headers middleware sets a restrictive Content-Security-Policy on **every** response (it is registered as `app.use("*", securityHeadersMiddleware())`):

```ts
// packages/api/src/middleware/security.middleware.ts:151
ctx.header("Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'");
```

The docs page violates this policy in two ways:

```html
<!-- packages/api/src/routes/docs.ts:253-265 -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/swagger-ui-dist@5/swagger-ui.css" />
...
<script src="https://unpkg.com/swagger-ui-dist@5/swagger-ui-bundle.js"></script>
<script>
  SwaggerUIBundle({ url: "${specUrl}", dom_id: "#swagger-ui", ... });
</script>
```

`script-src 'self'` blocks both the cross-origin `unpkg.com` bundle and the inline `<script>` bootstrap, and `default-src 'self'` blocks the cross-origin stylesheet. The browser refuses to load the script and run the inline initializer, so the Swagger UI never renders.

## Impact

The interactive API documentation served at `/api/docs` is non-functional in any standards-compliant browser — the page loads an empty `#swagger-ui` container with CSP violation errors in the console. The feature exists but cannot be used. **Medium** severity (broken developer-facing feature; no security loss since the CSP correctly stays strict on the API).

## Required Fix

1. Scope a relaxed CSP to the docs route only (e.g. allow `https://unpkg.com` for `script-src`/`style-src` and add a nonce or hash for the inline bootstrap), keeping the strict policy on all API routes.
2. Prefer eliminating the inline script (move the initializer to a served static file) and/or self-host the Swagger assets so no CDN or `unsafe-inline` is required.
3. Add a test asserting the `/api/docs` response carries a CSP that permits its own assets.

## References

- MDN — Content-Security-Policy `script-src`: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/script-src
- OWASP — Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Content_Security_Policy_Cheat_Sheet.html

title: Central error handler discards `ValidationError.details`, hiding which field failed
`/api/auth/login` accepts any credentials and mints a privileged token
CSRF cookie is never marked `Secure`; the agent passes no CSRF config
No `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException` handlers; shutdown closes no resources
JWT secret has no minimum-strength validation and silently falls back to a random UUID
body:
## Description

The JWT signing secret is an optional string with no length/strength constraint:

```ts
// configs/config.schema.ts:49-53
export const securityConfigSchema = z.object({
  jwt_secret: z.string().optional(),
  rate_limit_window: z.number().int().positive().default(900000),
  rate_limit_max: z.number().int().positive().default(100),
});
```

When it is omitted, the agent substitutes a per-process random UUID:

```ts
// apps/agent/src/index.ts:143
jwtSecret: validated.security.jwt_secret ?? crypto.randomUUID(),
```

So (a) an operator may configure a trivially weak secret (e.g. `"secret"`) with no validation, and (b) if no secret is set, a fresh random UUID is generated on **every** start.

## Impact

Two problems. First, a weak HS256 secret is brute-forceable offline, allowing token forgery — there is no guard against short/low-entropy secrets. Second, the silent `randomUUID()` fallback means the signing key changes on every restart, so all previously-issued tokens become invalid (users are logged out on each deploy/restart) and a `randomUUID` (122 bits, but not intended or documented as a signing key) is used without warning. **Low** severity (defaults/validation hardening) given the dev-stage auth, but it should be fixed before production.

## Required Fix

1. Enforce a minimum length/entropy on `jwt_secret` in the schema (e.g. `z.string().min(32)`).
2. Make the missing-secret behavior explicit: in production, refuse to start without a configured secret rather than generating an ephemeral one; in dev, log a clear warning that tokens will not survive restart.
3. Document the requirement to set a stable, high-entropy `jwt_secret`.

## References

- OWASP — JSON Web Token Cheat Sheet (key strength): https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/JSON_Web_Token_for_Java_Cheat_Sheet.html
- CWE-326: Inadequate Encryption Strength: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/326.html
- CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements (analogous weak-secret class): https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/521.html

title: Auth skip-list uses unbounded `/api/docs` prefix and contains a dead `/api/health` rule
body:
## Description

The auth middleware's skip-list matches the docs path with an unbounded `startsWith`:

```ts
// packages/api/src/middleware/auth.middleware.ts:71-78
if (
  ctx.req.path === "/api/health" ||
  ctx.req.path === "/" ||
  ctx.req.path.startsWith("/api/auth/") ||
  ctx.req.path.startsWith("/api/docs")
) {
  return next();
}
```

`startsWith("/api/docs")` matches any path with that prefix — including `/api/docs-internal`, `/api/docsadmin`, etc. — not just `/api/docs` and `/api/docs/*`. Separately, `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` defines `"/api/health": [...]` (`auth.middleware.ts:36`), but `/api/health` is unconditionally skipped here at line 72 before any permission check, so that map entry is dead. (The mirrored CSRF skip-list at `csrf.middleware.ts:81` similarly hard-codes `/api/health`, which is a `GET`-only route already skipped by the safe-method check.)

## Impact

The unbounded prefix means a future route whose name merely starts with `/api/docs` would unintentionally bypass authentication. The dead `/api/health` permission entry is misleading dead code that suggests health is access-controlled when it is in fact always public. **Low** severity (latent bypass surface + dead/misleading config; no current exploit since no such routes exist).

## Required Fix

1. Match the docs path exactly: use `path === "/api/docs" || path.startsWith("/api/docs/")` instead of the bare prefix.
2. Remove the dead `"/api/health"` entry from `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` (or stop unconditionally skipping it) so the intent is unambiguous.
3. Add a test that a path like `/api/docs-internal` is NOT auth-exempt.

## References

- OWASP Top 10 2021 — A01:2021 Broken Access Control: https://owasp.org/Top10/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/
- CWE-697: Incorrect Comparison: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/697.html
